ANSWER:

**Helper wrapping secret detection:** `check_secret` (in `src/memory/guard.rs`), which calls `secret_kind` (also in `src/memory/guard.rs`). `secret_kind` runs named regex patterns from the `SECRETS` static and a high-entropy token detector (`LONG_TOKEN` + `looks_random`).

**Fields `check_secret` is applied to** (all inside the `check` function, `src/memory/guard.rs:134–243`):
1. `text` (line 146) — the main claim body
2. `subject` (line 156) — the person/thing the memory is about
3. `key` (line 160) — the slot key
4. each `tag` (line 172) — per-tag in the loop
5. each `ref` (line 184) — per-ref in the loop
6. `source` (line 198) — attribution field

**Files and functions involved:**

| File | Function | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `src/memory/guard.rs` | `secret_kind` | Core detector: named-credential regexes + entropy heuristic |
| `src/memory/guard.rs` | `check_secret` | Thin wrapper that formats the refusal message and calls `secret_kind` |
| `src/memory/guard.rs` | `check` | Entry point for validating a full `Remember` request; calls `check_secret` on every user-supplied text field listed above |

**Affected validation sites if the credential check changes:** Any change to `secret_kind` or `check_secret` propagates to all six field checks inside `check` (`text`, `subject`, `key`, each tag, each ref, `source`). The `check` function is the sole caller of `check_secret`, and `check_secret` is the sole caller of `secret_kind`, so there is exactly one chain: `check` → `check_secret` → `secret_kind`.

CONFIDENCE: high
